**1/5 stars — Stackhouse Cloud at Bridger Bend Community Library**

Bridger Bend Community Library serves about 2,300 active cardholders from one branch with two full-time staff and volunteers. We signed a three-year Stackhouse Cloud contract in June 2026 at $14,200 per year. Our migration went live October 19.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only offline on one laptop, and our holds queue—about 640 holds—was wiped. We opened a support ticket 12 days ago. We’ve received three replies, each saying the issue has been “escalated to engineering,” but we still don’t have a working circulation system or a clear resolution timeline.

The effects are not abstract. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up held large-print Westerns. We had no record of his hold and sent him home without the books. One of our volunteers is recording checkouts on index cards.

Our experience also differs from what we understood we were buying. The sales representative promised “a dedicated migration specialist”; in practice, we had a shared inbox. The software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is honestly better than our old system. Our concern is not the product idea. It’s the support and follow-through when a small library has a serious problem.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and our library line item is on the agenda. I would like a named senior person at Stackhouse to call me this week and provide a concrete plan and timeline for restoring circulation and addressing the lost holds. I’ll update this review if the issue is resolved.

For other library directors considering Stackhouse: ask for support response times and escalation commitments in writing before you sign, and ask who will be accountable during migration and after go-live. Based on our experience so far, I can’t recommend the service. One star for now; I would revisit that rating if Stackhouse fixes the problem.
